lists.content:
A Deployment Strategist at Istari is the single accountable owner of a customer program's outcome. You will embed with a small team of forward deployed engineers on one flagship program, or a small set of lighter engagements, and you will decide what matters: which problems the team attacks and in what order, what each demonstration, technical interchange, or test event has to prove, and how the deployment becomes something the customer cannot imagine operating without. Some days that means a working session with a prime's chief engineer. Other days it means briefing a program executive on why a digital thread changes their schedule risk, or reading the room after a review board and knowing exactly which conversation needs to happen next.

On our largest federal programs, you also carry the formal Program Manager designation as contract key personnel. You are the government program office's day-to-day peer, and your name is on every deliverable commitment we make. You will have support from a shared Program Operations team  that helps to assemble reports, format deliverables, and work the submission machinery behind you – but you answer for all of it. Your hours go to the outcome and to what the program becomes next, not to the tracker.

You are not the primary builder here; we hire Forward Deployed Engineers for that, and your job is never to stand between them and the customer. You do need enough technical range that engineers trust your judgment and customers trust your answers. There is no fixed path into this role and no single background that produces a great Deployment Strategist. We are looking for people who would rather own the result than the process, and the more ownership you take, the more you will be given.

• Own the outcome of a program end to end: define what success means, choose the problems worth solving and the order to solve them in, and set what each milestone has to prove.

  • Embed with government and industry customers to understand their mission, their constraints, and their politics, and build relationships from end users to program executives that make a deployment durable.

  • Serve as named Program Manager on major federal programs: carry the program narrative through status reports, technical interchange meetings, and formal review boards, and stand accountable for every contract commitment.

  • Set direction and priorities for a small Forward Deployed Engineering team without intermediating between engineers and users, and protect their time from everything that is not the work.

  • Own the growth thesis: option years, follow-ons, and expansions grow out of delivered outcomes, and they are your responsibility to shape from inside the relationship.

  • Feed what you learn in the field back into product and engineering, so the platform gets better for every customer, not just the one in front of you.

  • Work day-to-day at or travel to customer sites, test events, hackathons, and program milestones as needed, typically domestic.

lists.text: Qualifications / Who thrives in this role
lists.content:
We hire for judgment, curiosity, and a bias toward action more than for a specific degree or years of experience. That said, people who do well in this role tend to share a few things:

  • A track record of owning an outcome with no formal authority over the people delivering it, and finding that energizing rather than alarming.

  • Insider fluency in the following customer domain… the kind that comes from having lived it, along with a clear view of what is broken in how that world works today.

    • Domain: air platform development and the lifecycle behind it — the research-to-transition pipeline for aerospace vehicles, autonomy, and propulsion; the acquisition, certification, and sustainment world that carries a weapon system from requirement to retirement; and the enterprise push to make digital engineering, model sharing, and digital threads real across all of it.

  • Technical conversancy across modeling and simulation, MBSE, digital threads, software development, and/or agentic design: enough to interrogate an engineering claim and be credible doing it, not necessarily enough to build it yourself.

  • Product sense, because this role sits closer to product management than to project management: knowing what to build next and what not to build at all, and telling the difference between a request that serves one user and a capability that belongs in the platform.

  • The range to brief a program executive in the morning and pair with an engineer in the afternoon.

  • An instinct for reading rooms and organizational dynamics, because adoption is won in the customer's org chart as much as in the software.

  • Comfort operating with incomplete information and shifting requirements, and the initiative to define next steps without being told.

    •  

    Preferred, not required

  • Highly desired: Experience in a forward deployed, deployment strategist, or field delivery role at a technology or defense company.

  • A prior key personnel Program Manager designation on a DoD or NASA contract, or time inside a government program office, uniformed or civilian.

  • Working familiarity with government contracting mechanics: deliverable cadences, milestone reviews, option years, and what a contracting officer cares about.

  • A track record of converting delivery into growth: an option year exercised, an expansion won, a pilot that became a program of record.

  • Eligibility to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance, given the classified and controlled environments this role supports.

You will work directly with the executives and engineers building the company, not through layers of process. You will see your work reach real programs and real missions quickly – the outcomes you own here end in test events and fielded systems, not slide decks – and you will have room to shape a role that does not yet have a fixed definition. This is a small team solving a problem that matters, and we are looking for people who want to build the next chapter of it with us.

Federal Pre-Sales Solutions Architect
Remote w/ travel (25-30%)
Reports to: Director of Sales
About Us
Istari Digital is a high-growth technology company enabling the next generation of AI-native engineering across aerospace, defense, and industrial enterprises. Our infrastructure platform orchestrates data across tools, organizations, and classification levels—removing barriers that limit digital engineering—and empowers customers to modernize mission-critical workflows and unlock meaningful ROI from digital transformation at scale.
To support rapid growth in federal markets, we are expanding our technical go-to-market team. This role is critical to enabling how customers understand, adopt, and operationalize Istari infrastructure to address mission critical challenges. 
Position Overview
The Solutions Architect is the technical authority for how Istari enables modern digital engineering workflows across federal and commercial missions. This role partners closely with engineering leaders, program teams, and account executives to understand how engineering data is created, shared, governed, and operationalized across tools, organizations, and security boundaries—and to architect Istari as the connective infrastructure that makes those workflows possible.
You will lead engineering-centric discovery, design workflow-driven solution architectures, and deliver compelling technical narratives that resonate with engineers, program managers, and digital engineering leadership. While you will advise on secure deployment patterns, your primary focus is enabling new ways of working: faster collaboration, reusable data, cross-program visibility, and measurable mission impact.
Account Executives own account strategy, opportunity qualification, and overall deal execution.
Solutions Architects own technical credibility, engineering workflow alignment, and solution viability—ensuring Istari is positioned as foundational digital engineering infrastructure, not just another tool or deployment.
Together, these roles form Istari’s growth engine by aligning mission needs, engineering realities, and platform capabilities into winning capture strategies.

lists.content:
Engineering Workflow Discovery & Mission Understanding

  • Lead discovery sessions with engineering teams to understand design, analysis, simulation, integration, and sustainment workflows.

  • Analyze how data flows across CAD, CAE, PLM, MBSE, simulation, and custom engineering tools.

  • Identify friction points such as broken handoffs, siloed data, limited reuse, and cross-program collaboration challenges.

  • Understand mission context, program structure, and organizational boundaries that shape how engineering work gets done.

  • Translate engineering pain points into Istari-enabled workflow architectures and value narratives.

    • Engineering-Centric Solution Architecture

  • Architect Istari solutions that orchestrate engineering tools, data models, and workflows across programs and organizations.

  • Design patterns for engineering data versioning, traceability, access control, and reuse.

  • Define how Istari integrates into existing toolchains rather than replacing them.

  • Ensure solution designs support engineering velocity, collaboration, and program outcomes—not just technical correctness.

  • Incorporate secure deployment considerations (cloud, on-prem, hybrid) as constraints within engineering-first designs.

    • Demo Delivery, Technical Storytelling & Value Translation

  • Own end-to-end demo preparation and delivery for prospects

  • Tailor demos to mission-specific scenarios, data flows, engineering tools, and classification requirements.

  • Build repeatable demo environments and customize them for unique use cases across DoD, IC, and federal civilian agencies. 

  • Collaborate with AEs to craft compelling technical narratives that articulate the “why,” not just the “how,” of Istari.

  • Capture demo feedback to refine content, improve demo flows, and influence roadmap priorities.

    • Pre-Sales Engagement & Technical Validation

  • Lead whiteboarding sessions focused on engineering workflows, data movement, and collaboration patterns.

  • Develop lightweight proofs of value that validate engineering integrations and workflow improvements.

  • Partner with Account Executives to quantify engineering impact (cycle time, reuse, coordination, risk reduction).

  • Articulate a clear technical path from initial workflow validation to production-scale adoption.

    • Security, Compliance & Infrastructure Expertise

  • Design engineering workflows that respect classification boundaries without breaking collaboration or continuity.

  • Advise on deployment patterns that enable cross-domain engineering while aligning with federal security requirements.

  • Partner with cybersecurity and infrastructure stakeholders to balance risk management with engineering productivity.

    • Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to translate real-world engineering needs into roadmap inputs.

  • Partner with Cybersecurity and Customer Success to ensure solutions scale beyond initial use cases.

  • Support federal capture efforts by shaping teaming strategies, solution architectures, and technical win themes.

  • Contribute reusable workflow patterns, demo assets, and technical documentation to scale the federal GTM motion.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience).

    • Experience

  • 5–10+ years in solutions architecture, systems engineering, pre-sales engineering, or technical consulting for complex engineering or infrastructure software.

  • Experience supporting federal missions (DoD, IC, national labs, or defense primes).

  • Hands-on experience working with engineering tools, workflows, or digital engineering environments.

  • Experience leading technical demos and customer-facing engineering discussions.

    • Skills & Capabilities

  • Deep ability to understand and articulate engineering workflows and data lifecycles.

  • Strong technical storytelling skills—able to translate complex engineering concepts into mission-relevant narratives.

  • Comfort whiteboarding workflows, toolchains, and data movement with engineering stakeholders.

  • Ability to design secure, distributed systems that support engineering collaboration.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills with sales, product, and engineering teams.

    • Preferred Experience

  • Background in aerospace, defense, or mission-critical engineering environments.

  • Familiarity with CAD/CAE, PLM, MBSE, simulation pipelines, or engineering data platforms.

  • Experience supporting sales efforts or technical win strategy.

• Shape the future of digital engineering across the DoD and national security ecosystem.

  • Lead the technical motion at the intersection of AI, engineering infrastructure, and multi-domain collaboration.

  • Work directly engineering leadership and mission stakeholders on high-impact deployments.

  • Influence the product roadmap through real mission needs and demo feedback.

  • Join a high-trust, mission-driven team building transformative technology.

descriptionPlain:
We are seeking a Senior Security Engineer to lead and advance the security tooling that tests and validates our software against compliance and cybersecurity standards. In this role, you will ensure our toolchain is consistently enforced, highly trustworthy, and continuously enhanced as our products, customer base, and regulatory requirements expand. You will also be a key early contributor as we design and implement our application security and security operations functions.  
You will be the technical authority for how security checks are configured, tuned, and enforced across our software development lifecycle (SDLC). You will translate compliance and Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements into automated, risk-based controls that give engineers fast, actionable feedback early in development. Your expertise in AI-based automation will be key to success. The goal is a pipeline calibrated to the speed of organizational need: secure by default, automated wherever possible, and supported by clear human review when automation flags risk.
On the other end of the SDLC, you will help implement automated and manual pen-testing and other security-related testing capabilities across a range of deployment environments. You will help develop our security operations capabilities with faster and more automated incident response and incident management. Applying an AI-first approach to these functions will enable faster, more efficient, higher-quality outcomes. 
This role supports regulated and security-sensitive environments, including systems hosted for Government customers, and partners closely with engineering, product, and cybersecurity leadership.

lists.content:
Own and evolve the security toolchain

  • Serve as the technical owner of our pipeline security tooling, including static application security testing (SAST), software composition analysis (SCA), secrets detection, container scanning, and artifact signing

  • Assess tooling effectiveness and coverage, identify gaps, and recommend and lead improvements, consolidation, or replacement as needs evolve

  • Develop automated and manual pen-testing capabilities with rapid feedback loops into the engineering process.

  • Help mature the security operations and incident response capabilities of the company.

  • Define the long-term roadmap for security tooling and processes in partnership with Cybersecurity and Engineering leadership

    • Tune controls to compliance requirements

  • Translate National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, and RMF control requirements into enforceable pipeline gates, thresholds, and policies

  • Evolve and maintain risk-based pass/fail criteria that balance security assurance with delivery speed and minimize false positives

  • Ensure tooling outputs produce assessor-ready evidence that supports authorizations, continuous monitoring, and audits

  • Own the exception and manual-review process for findings that fail automated checks, so decisions are documented and traceable

    • Enforce integrity and consistency

  • Ensure security results cannot be bypassed or tampered with, including enforcement of artifact signing, signature verification before deployment, commit signing, branch protection, and repository rulesets

  • Automate the creation and maintenance of software bills of materials (SBOMs) and vulnerability exploitability exchange (VEX) data for delivered software

    • Drive shift-left adoption

  • Move security checks to the earliest practical point (developer workstation, pre-commit, pull request, etc.)

  • Partner with engineering teams to embed security into their workflows, supported by clear standards and guidance, so the secure path is the easy path

  • Apply artificial intelligence (AI) tooling to accelerate vulnerability triage, remediation, and security automation, and evaluate emerging AI capabilities for the toolchain

• 7+ years in DevSecOps, application security, security operations and incident response, and general security engineering, including at least 3 years owning security tooling in continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines

  • Deep hands-on experience configuring, tuning, and enforcing SAST, SCA, secrets detection, and container scanning tools in production pipelines, including risk-based gates, vulnerability thresholds, and exception processes

  • Demonstrated experience mapping security tooling and pipeline controls to NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, or RMF requirements, and producing evidence for assessments or authorizations

  • Track record of evaluating, selecting, or evolving security tooling, and influencing engineering teams without direct authority

  • Scripting or automation experience in Python, Bash, or similar

  • Security+ or equivalent Department of Defense (DoD) 8140 qualifying certification, or ability to obtain within 2 months of hire

  • U.S. citizen residing and working in the U.S.

• Familiarity with tools such as GitHub, Argo CD, JFrog, and Snyk

  • Experience in DoD software factory or Government DevSecOps environments (for example, Platform One, Iron Bank, or Big Bang)

  • Experience supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) efforts, including control assessment and Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) management

  • Experience with software supply chain integrity and policy-as-code practices, such as artifact signing, signature verification, SBOMs, Open Policy Agent (OPA), or Kyverno

  • Experience applying AI and large language model (LLM) tools to security engineering, such as AI-assisted triage, code review, or remediation

  • Experience with penetration testing tools, processes, strategies. 

  • Familiarity with the cloud and container environments where pipelines run and are deployed (for example, Github, Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS)

  • Advanced certifications such as CISSP, SecurityX (CASP+), or GIAC (GSSP, GCSA, or similar)

  • Active security clearance (Top Secret highly desired)

descriptionPlain:
[ABOUT ISTARI DIGITAL]
Istari is a digital engineering software company enabling our customers to turn the physical world into the digital to accomplish their specific mission or business objectives.

Istari was founded with the vision of making open, scalable digital engineering ecosystems a reality – where new technologies and systems are created digitally, free from the real-world constraints of costs and schedules. We are creating the world’s best engineering model sharing platform, allowing our customers to simply and securely integrate their models across different engineering disciplines, organizations, and security levels.

At Istari, we are passionate about our mission of creating the world's first open and scalable industrial metaverse. Whether our customers are designing prototypes, performing virtual testing, or training AI and autonomy for complex systems, we know that going digital will save them time, resources, and reduce their environmental impact.  

While we are a distributed team with most team-members working remotely, we place an emphasis on staying connected and collaborative, prioritizing in-person opportunities to build trust as a team. At Istari, we still believe that trust is best built in-person. To do this, we have an engineering headquarters in Cambridge, MA for focused technical development and several times per year we gather for an off-site that allows us to develop our professional skills and our team relationships.

[VALUES]
At Istari, we live by our values, which include:

- Focus is rewarded. Finish is remembered. 
- Facts are friendly. Even when they are not fun.
- Fellowship is fundamental. Make others successful.

Equal Opportunity 
Istari is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, or disability status.



The Strategic Partnerships Lead is responsible for building, managing, and operationalizing Istari’s ecosystem of strategic technology partners—particularly engineering tool providers, channel partners and prime partners pursuing large federal captures—to support capture efforts and long-term market expansion.
 
This role sits at the intersection of partnerships, sales, and technical strategy. You will develop teaming relationships, shape joint value propositions, and support capture teams by positioning Istari and its partners as differentiated, mission-aligned solutions for complex government programs.
 
Successful candidates bring credibility across federal teaming environments, strong technical fluency in engineering software ecosystems, and the ability to translate partnerships into concrete capture advantages.

The Strategic Partnerships Lead is responsible for building, managing, and operationalizing Istari’s ecosystem of strategic technology partners—particularly engineering tool providers, channel partners and prime partners pursuing large federal captures—to support capture efforts and long-term market expansion.
 
This role sits at the intersection of partnerships, sales, and technical strategy. You will develop teaming relationships, shape joint value propositions, and support capture teams by positioning Istari and its partners as differentiated, mission-aligned solutions for complex government programs.
 
Successful candidates bring credibility across federal teaming environments, strong technical fluency in engineering software ecosystems, and the ability to translate partnerships into concrete capture advantages.

lists.content:
• Strategic Partnership Development: Identify, evaluate, and establish strategic relationships with engineering tool providers, data platforms, and adjacent technology partners (e.g., CAD/CAE, digital engineering, security, observability, data infrastructure). Build executive and working-level relationships across partner organizations, including BD, product, and technical leadership. Define partnership models spanning teaming agreements, joint solutions, go-to-market alignment, and long-term platform integration. Define metrics for joint-GTM motions and track contribution to revenue growth.
  • Federal Teaming & Capture Support: Support Federal capture teams by developing teaming strategies aligned to specific programs, agencies, and mission needs. Shape partner-inclusive value propositions that clearly articulate Istari’s differentiated role within broader solution stacks. Contribute to capture planning, whitepapers, RFI/RFP responses, and oral strategies where partner alignment is critical. Help identify incumbents, competitors, and ecosystem gaps within target programs and advise on optimal teaming configurations.
  • Joint Value Proposition & Solution Strategy: Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and Solution Architects to define how partner technologies integrate with Istari’s platform. Translate technical integrations into compelling narratives around mission impact, program risk reduction, and operational outcomes. Ensure partner positioning reinforces Istari as foundational digital engineering infrastructure—not a point solution.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Federal Account Executives, BD, and Sales Leadership to align partnerships with active pursuits and pipeline. Provide market, partner, and competitive insights to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap priorities. Coordinate with Marketing and Sales Enablement on partner messaging, collateral, and field readiness (as needed).

• 6–10+ years of experience in engagement management, strategic partnerships, federal BD, capture support, or ecosystem-focused roles.
  • Experience operating in DoD, federal civilian, or national security markets with exposure to formal teaming and capture processes.
  • Background working with engineering software, data platforms, infrastructure tools, or highly technical B2B solutions.
  • Demonstrated success translating partnerships into tangible capture or revenue outcomes.
  • Strong understanding of federal teaming dynamics, partner incentives, and capture mechanics.
  • Ability to engage credibly with technical, product, and business stakeholders across multiple organizations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable contributing to capture artifacts and executive-level discussions.
  • Strategic mindset paired with a bias toward execution in a fast-moving, early-stage environment.
  • High ownership, autonomy, and comfort operating with ambiguity.
  • Team Player
  • U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required (due to the nature of our work with the Department of Defense)

• Experience partnering with or selling alongside engineering tool vendors (CAD/CAE, PLM, digital engineering, security, data infrastructure).
  • Familiarity with digital engineering, model-based systems engineering (MBSE), or engineering data workflows.
  • Prior experience supporting major defense primes, system integrators, or large federal programs.
  • Background in aerospace, defense, or national security technology ecosystems.
